issues.description: Conditional class registration sits outside the class block with no blank line, complecting class definition with version-gated registration
issues.detail: The `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11): Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` is glued to the class with no separating blank line, and rebinds the class name as a side effect. The data (which math functions exist per Python version) is tangled into the control flow of module load. A small data table mapping (name, min_version) to intrinsic would decompose this.

issues.description: Missing `import sys` in numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py where `sys.version_info` is now referenced
issues.detail: The diff adds `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` guards in two impl files but does not show a corresponding `import sys`. If `sys` is not already imported at module top, these modules will NameError on load for every Python version. EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: the version-gate pattern was copied without checking the precondition.

issues.description: Version-gating is duplicated across three files; the rule about which functions exist when should be one piece of data
issues.detail: Three separate `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` branches now encode the same fact in mathdecl, cpython/mathimpl, and np/math/mathimpl. The fact (math.exp2 exists from 3.11) is a value; it has been complected into module-load control flow in three places. One predicate or registry would make this simple instead of merely easy.

issues.description: Test reuses `exp` x_values verbatim without exercising values where exp2 differs meaningfully from exp
issues.detail: TDD-AS-DESIGN: the test was cloned from `test_exp` and inherits its inputs. exp2(x) = 2**x has interesting behavior at integer x (exact powers of two) and large x where it differs from e**x; none of that is probed. A small data table of (input, expected) for known powers would test the actual semantics.

issues.description: Inconsistent version-check mechanism: `sys.version_info` in source files, `PYVERSION` in tests
issues.detail: The codebase already has `numba.core.utils.PYVERSION` (used in the test). Source files use raw `sys.version_info` instead. Two ways to spell the same fact is incidental complexity; pick one. Prefer the existing PYVERSION constant so the version policy lives in one place.

issues.description: Release note file missing trailing newline and underline length is fragile
issues.detail: `docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst` ends without a newline and the underline is hand-counted to match the title. Minor incidental noise. Add the newline; lint may catch the underline.

review.summary: The change is small and the intent is clear, but it spreads a single fact — "math.exp2 exists from Python 3.11" — across three modules as imperative version-gate branches rather than as data in one place. That is the classic easy-not-simple move: copy the surrounding pattern, gate with sys.version_info, ship. Two of those files likely need an `import sys` that the diff does not show, which would NameError on load. The test was cloned from test_exp and inherits its inputs without probing the values where exp2 actually differs from exp (integer powers of two). Decompose: one PYVERSION-keyed registry of (name, intrinsic, min_version), and test the semantics, not the shape of the neighboring test.
